title: Runtime LTS: publish artifact checksums + provenance metadata (verification docs included)
author: Sahana Iyer
body:
## Context
Enterprise Private + Dedicated customers asked for verifiable, auditable runtime artifacts for the LTS channel (checksums, provenance, and a documented verification procedure). Today we publish images/tarballs but do not consistently ship machine-readable metadata that maps artifacts back to a commit + build environment.

This PR adds:
- SHA256 checksum generation for runtime artifacts (images + tarballs) with a stable manifest format
- Provenance metadata (build inputs + source commit + builder identity) emitted as a JSON sidecar per artifact
- A small verification guide aimed at enterprise distribution (how to validate checksums and map artifacts back to a git SHA/tag)

This is a prerequisite for Private installer pinning + "auditable release artifacts" in the LTS spec.

## What’s included
### 1) Checksum manifests
For each runtime release build we now produce:
- `<artifact>.sha256` (single-line sha256sum output)
- `runtime-artifacts-<version>.checksums.txt` (aggregate manifest)

Manifest format is intentionally compatible with standard tooling:
- generated via `sha256sum` style output (`<sha>  <filename>`)
- sorted by filename for stable diffs

### 2) Provenance JSON sidecars
Each artifact also gets a provenance sidecar:
- `<artifact>.provenance.json`

Fields included (v1):
- `source_repo`, `source_ref`, `source_commit`
- `build_id` (CI run id) + `builder` (workflow name)
- `created_at` (UTC)
- `dockerfile_digest` (when applicable)
- `toolchain` (compiler/tool versions we already pin in CI)

NOTE: This is not a full SLSA attestation yet; it’s a deterministic, auditable metadata block that we can evolve. (Follow-up will evaluate cosign/GitHub provenance once signing key management is finalized.)

### 3) Docs: verification procedure
Adds `docs/runtime/lts/artifact-verification.md` that covers:
- verifying aggregate checksum manifests
- verifying individual `.sha256` files
- validating provenance fields (commit/tag match, build id match)
- how Private customers can store manifests in their change-control/audit systems

## Implementation details
- New script: `tools/release/generate_artifact_metadata.py`
  - Inputs: artifact directory + release version + git commit
  - Outputs: `.sha256`, `.checksums.txt`, `.provenance.json`
- Updated release CI workflow for release branches to call metadata generation after packaging and before publish.
- Publish step now uploads metadata files alongside artifacts to the same release bucket/path.

## Example outputs
Aggregate checksum manifest snippet:
`e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855  runtime-1.18.1-lts-linux-amd64.tar.gz`

Provenance snippet:
`{"source_repo":"redwood","source_ref":"refs/tags/runtime-1.18.1-lts","source_commit":"3f2c9b1e...","builder":"release-ci/runtime-release","build_id":"12988421","created_at":"2025-03-02T18:44:10Z","toolchain":"cuda=12.4, gcc=11.4, python=3.11"}`

## Rollout / compatibility
- No runtime behavior changes.
- Hosted/Dedicated unaffected except improved artifacts.
- Private: installer/helm work will consume these manifests in follow-up PRs (ENG-4827 / ENG-4828).

## Security / threat model notes
- Checksums protect against accidental corruption and enable customer-side validation.
- Provenance is intended to support auditability and internal change control.
- This PR does not add signing. We will treat signing as a separate step once key custody / CI access controls are finalized.

## Checklist
- [x] Works for main + release/* branches
- [x] Metadata generation is deterministic for identical inputs
- [x] CI uploads metadata to the same destination as artifacts
- [x] Docs added for enterprise verification
- [x] Release eng reviewed

## Follow-ups
- Add optional signing of manifests (cosign or internal KMS-backed signing)
- Extend provenance schema to include SBOM pointer once SBOM generation lands for LTS builds
- Wire Private installer to enforce checksum verification by default

commits: release-ci: generate sha256 manifests for runtime artifacts
release-ci: add provenance sidecar JSON for each published artifact
docs: add enterprise verification guide for LTS artifacts
tools: add metadata generator script + tests
ci_summary: release-runtime / build-runtime-artifacts (pass); unit-tests (pass); lint (pass); release-branch-smoke (pass). Initial failure: publish step missing write permission to metadata path on release buckets; fixed by adjusting scoped token + rerun.
review_conversation: Connor O'Brien (review): Can we ensure the checksum manifest is stable across runners? Sorting + consistent newline handling matters for diffs and for customer change-control.
Sahana Iyer (author): Yep. Updated generator to sort by filename and force LF newlines. Added a unit test that snapshots manifest output ordering.
Dr. Aisha Rahman (review): Please avoid claiming this is SLSA provenance in docs. Also add a note about trust boundaries (checksum != signature).
Sahana Iyer (author): Updated docs to call it "provenance metadata" and added a section clarifying checksum vs signing, plus a follow-up for signing once key custody is resolved.
Bruno Silva (review): For Private installer consumption, we’ll need a single URL we can embed. Can we keep the aggregate manifest name consistent across patches?

Sahana Iyer (author): Kept it versioned but stable: `runtime-artifacts-<version>.checksums.txt` plus per-artifact `.sha256`. We can also add a `latest.checksums.txt` alias later if needed; not doing that in this PR to avoid confusing caching behavior.
Sean Gallagher (review): CI incident: publish permissions. Confirm we’re not widening bucket write access for workflows beyond release branches.
Sahana Iyer (author): Confirmed. Token scope is restricted to the `runtime-releases/*` prefix and the workflow only runs on `release/*` and tag builds. Added a note in the workflow comments.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash after approvals from Release Eng + Security; backport to runtime-1.18-lts tracked separately for the first patch cut.
